clue.text: Like these down entries and calm our nerves, just a bit churned up

indicators.note: churned up says the letters of calm our, with the extra letter, are stirred into a new order
just a bit of the word nerves is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Someone stirred up by nerves tries to calm themselves, only slightly succeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just a bit' of nerves gives N; 'churned up' shuffles CALM OUR with that N.
explanation.definitionFit: Down entries in a grid are arranged vertically, in the form of columns, so they are columnar.

clue.text: Fungus perhaps mostly evenly dispersed

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered about, so the gathered letters are spread into a new order
evenly picks the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth and sixth, of the word mostly

explanation.surface: A puzzled note that something, maybe a fungus, is spread fairly uniformly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like it marks the fungus as an example, but it is anagram fodder. 'evenly' takes OTY from mOsTlY; 'dispersed' shuffles PERHAPS with OTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A saprophyte is an organism that feeds on decaying matter, as many fungi and moulds do.

clue.text: What's left for instance in puddled clay

indicators.note: in places the example abbreviation inside the reworked clay
puddled clay has been worked and mixed with water, so its letters are kneaded into another order

parts.note: EG, short for exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: Something remaining, an example perhaps, stuck in wet worked clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puddled' (worked into wet clay) is the anagram signal, giving LACY; 'in' sets the example abbreviation within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is what a deceased person has left to someone in a will.

clue.text: Cut out central section of rough drawings

indicators.note: only the central section of the word is kept, so the outer pairs of letters are dropped

parts.note: rough drawings are sketches

explanation.surface: An instruction to excise the middle part of some draft drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central section of' drops SK and ES from the ends of SKETCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave, cutting a design out of a surface with acid or a tool.

clue.text: Attire of doctor in conflict with honour

indicators.note: in places the doctor letters inside the conflict and honour pieces joined together

parts.note: a war is a conflict
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: The clothing of a medic caught up in a war who has also been decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a person's whole collection of clothes, their attire.

clue.text: Independent's new head of telesales? On the contrary

parts.note: I abbreviates Independent, and 's is kept as S

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of telesales

explanation.surface: Reads like a newspaper story about the Independent appointing a new head of sales, with a contrary twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's '?' and 'On the contrary' are the contradicting retort, as in 'It is!' – 'It isn't!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'isn't' contradicts an assertion, the same job as the phrase on the contrary.

clue.text: A metal splinter I picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted higher, so the letter I moves one place nearer the top

parts.note: a sliver is a splinter

explanation.surface: Someone describes collecting a metal shard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means earlier: the I of SLIVER moves one place up.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, symbol Ag.

clue.text: Five yoga exercises on European cruise

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: exercises suggests the letters of yoga being worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: An onboard fitness programme of yoga classes on a European cruise holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' turns YOGA into OYAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyage is a long journey by sea, such as a cruise.

clue.text: Broadcast mike in a van

indicators.note: in places the mike letter inside the van's name

parts.note: the Ford Transit is a common van in Britain
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A radio reporter broadcasting from a microphone inside an outside-broadcast van.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Transit is the best-known British van, so 'a van' can be TRANSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to send out a signal, the same as broadcast as a verb.

clue.text: Transcend extravagant endless pain

parts.note: outré means unconventional or extravagant

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut from the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Getting beyond a wild, never-ending agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last E of ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To outreach something is to exceed or go beyond it, which is to transcend it.

clue.text: District attorney initially thinks I have a case

parts.note: DA is the American abbreviation for district attorney

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of thinks

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A prosecutor muses that there is a legal case to answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal beside the attorney, but it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, marking the indirect object in Latin, German and other languages.

clue.text: Smart game to play outside

parts.note: snap is a simple card game

indicators.note: outside picks the outer letters of the word play

explanation.surface: A clever game to enjoy in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' gives PY, the outer letters of play.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy is used for stylish or sharp, as in a snappy dresser, so it means smart.

clue.text: How rook flapping by motorway gets a parasite

indicators.note: flapping, like a bird's wings, signals the letters of how rook are tossed about

parts.note: M designates a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A whimsical story of a rook flying beside a motorway catching a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' shuffles HOWROOK into HOOKWOR. British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hookworms are parasitic nematodes living in the intestines of their host.

clue.text: Many a white one's seen from rocky shore

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of shore are knocked into another order

explanation.surface: Breaking waves seen from a rocky coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' shuffles SHORE. White horses are waves with foaming crests; 'one's seen from' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: White horses are foam-crested waves, so many a white one is a horse in that idiom.

clue.text: Gnu edible when minced in boiled stew

indicators.note: in places the minced letters inside the boiled ones
boiled suggests stirring the letters of stew in the pot
minced means chopped up, so the letters of edible are rearranged

explanation.surface: A culinary tip: gnu becomes edible when minced into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Both cooking words, 'when minced' and 'boiled', are anagram signals, and 'in' sets one result inside the other. 'Gnu edible' reads as one phrase but Gnu alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu is another name for the wildebeest, an African antelope.

clue.text: Like a member of the military?

definitions.text: Like a member of the military?

parts.words: Like a member of the military?
parts.note: a member can be a limb, so the word read as limb plus the adjective ending means limb-like, while plainly it describes things soldierly

explanation.surface: Asking what quality a soldier has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' means a limb here: add -Y to make 'like an arm'. The plain sense is the adjective, as in an army uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Army is used attributively for things of the armed forces, such as army boots.

clue.text: At any time that is weird

parts.note: e'er, poetic for ever, means at any time
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A remark that something is always strange.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is the poetic short form of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange in a frightening way, a synonym of weird.

clue.text: Take food into doorway for begging

indicators.note: into places the eating word inside the doorway word

parts.note: an entry is a doorway or entrance
to eat is to take food

explanation.surface: Someone bringing food to a doorway to beg, like a mendicant.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun begging, as in an act of pleading, is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, an act of begging.

clue.text: Greeny-yellow mucus after wiping top of sleeve

indicators.note: wiping takes away a letter from the word for mucus

parts.note: slime is mucus

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of sleeve

explanation.surface: An unpleasant picture of green snot on a sleeve after a nose-wipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' gives S; 'after wiping' removes it from SLIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime is a bright yellowish-green colour, named after the citrus fruit.

clue.text: Wizard guy conceals all-American private intelligence

indicators.note: conceals means the man word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a guy is a man
a GI is an ordinary American private soldier
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A man hiding a secret: he is an American soldier working for intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' splits the guy word after its second letter. 'all-American' simply stresses that the private is a US soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician is a sorcerer who practises magic, which a wizard does.

clue.text: Half out of uniform ointment on cut leg's rough

indicators.note: out of says the picked letter leaves the ointment word, one of the pair it holds

parts.note: an unguent is an ointment

indicators.note: Half takes just the opening part of the word uniform, its first letter, since the ointment word holds that letter twice and only one goes
cut means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: the leg word, with its possessive ignored

explanation.surface: A gritty first-aid scene: ointment smeared on a cut leg through torn uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Uniform is U (NATO alphabet). UNGUENT has two Us, so 'Half' of them goes 'out of' it, giving UNGENT. 'cut' trims LEG to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungentle means harsh or not mild, which is rough.

clue.text: Vitamin in one way and another gives protection for a cold

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the in pieces enclose a and cold
one way means the word in is read in one direction, backwards in this case

parts.note: the word itself
and another means in read the other way, forwards
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A vitamin protecting you from a cold in one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: IN read 'one way' (NI) and 'another' (IN) surround A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Niacin, nicotinic acid, is vitamin B3.

clue.text: Security needed for place on the border

parts.note: PL abbreviates place, in addresses
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A security force needed for a location on a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security' is the noun: something pledged as surety.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is something given as security for a loan or promise.

clue.text: Royal Navy invested in value

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money goes into a fund, so the navy letter goes into the value word

parts.note: price is value

explanation.surface: Money put into the Royal Navy for its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Navy' looks like one unit, RN, but 'Royal' is the definition and only N is inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a royal, a member of a royal family.

clue.text: Struggle to keep dry in a load of hay?

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so the hay word holds the dry letters

parts.note: a bale is a bundled load of hay
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, or dry

explanation.surface: The effort of keeping a haystack dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means teetotal here, TT, not free of moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a hard struggle or fight.

clue.text: It's ending in aftermath

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the letters of aftermath

explanation.surface: Remarks that something concludes in its consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed limit or conclusion, as a pregnancy reaching term, so an ending.

clue.text: Proof of a base immorality around hideout

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: around means the vice word wraps the hideout word

parts.note: vice is immorality
a den is a hideout

explanation.surface: Evidence of low wickedness found around a criminals' hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like an adjective for low, but it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is what proves or supports a claim, so it is proof.

clue.text: Start off banquet as one at table

indicators.note: start off means the first letter is removed from the banquet word

parts.note: a feast is a banquet

explanation.surface: Kicking off a dinner as the guest at the head of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one at table' is a bridge player: the four seats are North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, East is one of the four players at the card table.

clue.text: Russian fighter speeds and leaves country

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
rates are speeds

explanation.surface: A Russian fighter pilot defecting at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To migrate is to move from one country or region to another.

clue.text: Charlie, like so often, needing us to go easy

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
as means like

indicators.note: to go means the us letters leave the so-often word

parts.note: usual means as so often happens

explanation.surface: Telling Charlie, as so often, to relax with us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' takes US from USUAL, leaving UAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual means relaxed and informal, an easy manner.
